stem:
In summer, Meera's family in Jaipur draws water from a well near their house. Rainwater from the rooftop is directed through pipes into the soil, so water keeps seeping into the ground. Even so, the level of water in the well falls lower every summer.
Which statement best explains why the groundwater level can fall even though water seeps into the ground?

options.text: Groundwater cannot fall while any water seeps into the ground.

teacher.key_rationale: Groundwater decreases when extraction (well use) plus reduced replenishment outweigh seepage; seepage alone does not guarantee a constant level. Option A reverses the relation (any seepage means no fall), B reverses cause (more seepage lowers level), D is a scope error (only underground lakes count as groundwater). Correct answer: extraction can exceed replenishment, so level falls.
